author: nshchego
title: Windows GPU unit tests job fails extracting OpenVINO packages due to locked tbb12.dll
signature: windows runner extract openvino packages expand-archive remove-item access to the path denied unauthorizedaccessexception locked dll file|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step failed: Expand-Archive could not overwrite tbb12.dll because PowerShell's Remove-Item raised UnauthorizedAccessException (file locked/permission denied).

root_cause: The 'Extract OpenVINO packages' step runs Expand-Archive -Force against an install directory that already contains tbb12.dll from a prior extraction/build step on the same Windows self-hosted runner. PowerShell's Expand-Archive -Force implementation removes pre-existing files before writing new ones; Remove-Item fails with UnauthorizedAccessException because tbb12.dll is still memory-mapped/locked by another process (most likely a lingering antivirus scan, a leftover process from a prior job on the same reused runner, or an open file handle from the build step). This is a transient Windows-runner file-locking issue, not caused by the merged PR's change (a GPU test-skip filter unrelated to packaging/extraction).
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires the specific Windows self-hosted runner state (locked DLL handle) and is not reliably reproducible locally. To reproduce conditions: on a Windows runner, pre-populate the install directory with tbb12.dll from a build, open a handle to it (e.g., leave an .exe linked against it running), then run 'Expand-Archive -Force' against an archive containing the same file.
recommended_actions: Add a retry-with-delay wrapper around the Expand-Archive/Remove-Item extraction step for Windows jobs to tolerate transient file locks (similar to patterns used for flaky file I/O on Windows runners).

Investigate whether antivirus (Windows Defender) real-time scanning or a lingering process from the 'Build' job is holding a handle on tbb12.dll immediately after extraction; consider adding a short sleep/garbage-collection or explicit process cleanup before extraction.
Consider using 7zip or robocopy-based extraction instead of Expand-Archive -Force, which handles locked destination files more gracefully (e.g., skip-if-identical or retry logic).

This is a recurring pattern (2nd occurrence) — escalate to the CI infrastructure team to investigate the Windows self-hosted runner pool for stale processes/AV locks rather than treating each occurrence as a one-off.
prevention_strategies: Wrap Windows archive-extraction steps with a retry loop (e.g., 3 attempts with short backoff) when Remove-Item/Expand-Archive fails with UnauthorizedAccessException, since transient file locks on shared Windows runners are common. Ensure build/test steps release file handles on DLLs (e.g., tbb12.dll) before the packaging/extraction job starts, and periodically recycle Windows runner images to clear stale locked handles.
